decisions.reason: The entire polished transcript was read independently. Kenzo, Riswynn, Delwath, Seeker and Wellby all act in play, matching the YAML PCs. The recording progresses from afternoon through a concurrent one-hour watch to about 7 pm; it supplies no calendar date contrary to the YAML single-day anchor. Historical dates, Vola’s captivity duration, and speculative plans do not advance the session. The visited-location list contains the connected dwarven outpost and Raven’s Hold, not the merely mentioned Karawa, Chardon or Drankor. Registered source IDs resolve; all six ancillary path proposals remain informational and do not alter source/date authority.

The 36-scene division preserves one contiguous range per scene, accounts for all 2875 UIDs, separates the two combats and main location changes, and correctly treats the two watches as concurrent. The three excluded blocks are accurately characterized as reconnection, wrap-up fatigue and scheduling, with no lost played event. Scene 23 has a concrete location/action error: u1750–u1753 describes Kenzo opening the barred route between the towers, not the companions entering the first tower. Correct its detail and summary without changing its range. Other regrouping positions remain appropriately broad; the connector has no forced vault match. Minor mixed table chatter may remain in scenes.

The wounded prisoner gives her name and is directly freed, healed, rescued and debriefed. The linked Vola page identifies the same Chardonian Society member. The two-sentence session overview reflects the source and does not import later biography; several genuine Vola lines support featured selections.

Vola explicitly names Agata Dustmother and attributes the relic search and captors to her. The alias resolves the vault page. The overview preserves Vola as the source and avoids importing the later-known hag identity or asserting direct presence.

Arcus is explicitly named; Vola recognizes him and identifies his Society membership. The linked page matches. The overview correctly attributes the death claim to Wellby rather than silently converting it into a new canonical death finding; this matters because the reference page describes petrification.

A distinctive cloaked, armed, speaking orc participates in the rescue conflict, casts darkness, threatens the party and dies. This individual merits an unresolved NPC card despite lacking a name; no speculative named vault match is supplied. Later attribution of service to Agata is explicitly sourced to Vola.

The exact named clan mark appears in Wellby’s report and on the apartment wall. The canonical clan page is the correct identity. Treating these as discussion/evidence of historical occupation avoids implying that the organization itself was physically present.

Vola’s initial reference to the Society is resolved by her later full name and explanation of its mission. The linked scholarly society is the correct organization. Its interactions stay mentioned rather than treating the meeting with Vola as contact with every member.

decisions.reason: The source explicitly describes the Great Library as a major institution and connects the relic hunters with it. The canonical page covers both institution and building, so organization is appropriate here. It remains distinct from the Society and is not included among visited locations.

Wellby presents and the party examines an unreadable dated hobgoblin logbook. It is a meaningful clue object, not ordinary treasure. The linked reference page’s first paragraph describes this outpost logbook; its separate Looseleaf Hobgoblin Journal section must not be conflated with this object. The current overview and interaction do not make that conflation.

evidence.vaultPath: Campaigns/Dunmari Frontier Campaign/Letters and Notes/Hobgoblin Notes from Raven's Hold.md

decisions.reason: A magical scroll is newly discovered concealed in the captain’s desk; its spell is explicitly unrecognized. The discovery meets item selection criteria. The unresolved label and absent vault match correctly preserve uncertainty without importing a later identity.

The complete private meeting stays one interaction across the brief downstairs check, while scenes retain the physical movement. Freeing, naming, reassurance and healing are directly supported. Star importance is appropriate. All four quotes are exact polished substrings; the introduction is DM narration and the color lines are Vola’s speech.

This continuous rescue/debrief is sensibly grouped across room changes and a short out-of-character pause. The primary passage carries the substantive conversation; the supporting passage retains return of her gear and relocation. The overview is one sentence and supported. The selected relic-race and empire quotes are Vola’s own words, not DM exposition or PC jokes.

The passage supports a mentioned, supporting role: Vola supplies Agata’s name, unknown nature, relic motives and connection to the three captors. The summary attributes this report and does not promote it to direct observation.

Wellby’s report and Vola’s reaction form the primary passage; her later statement of membership justifies the supporting passage from the same conversation. The quotation is the PC’s exact statement. The summary retains attribution and does not override the linked page’s petrified condition.
Kenzo sees the distinctive orc without engaging him, so observed is correct. The introduction quote is exact DM description and its range retains the complete contributing polished turn.

Direct combat belongs under interacted. The passage preserves the complete fight rather than fragmenting rounds. Darkness and death are supported, and both memorable threats are explicitly voiced by the orc in the DM’s narration. Supporting importance is reasonable in a rescue centered on Vola.
Vola explicitly says that the three slain captors served Agata. The orc is one of those three. This is a later report, correctly mentioned with cameo importance, rather than a new direct encounter.

Wellby shows marked coins and explains the tribal standard. The organization is meaningfully mentioned; the coins remain ordinary treasure without an item card. The supporting clarification remains within the same ongoing discussion.

The painted mark and captain’s possessions support historical Blackened Claw occupation. Mentioned avoids inferring present membership from a symbol. Joining the initial sighting and later search is reasonable for this small continuous exploration; the exact quote is descriptive introduction.

Vola asks whether the Society sent Kenzo, and he asks which Society. This brief first reference is distinct from the later debrief because Kenzo leaves and combat intervenes; cameo mentioned is supported.

Vola explicitly identifies the Society’s relic-recovery efforts and Arcus’s membership. The source is one coherent conversational passage. Supporting mentioned is appropriate, with no invented encounter with the institution.

The source connects the hunters with the library and separately establishes Kenzo’s existing recognition of the named Great Library. The secondary passage is useful identity/context support. The institution is discussed, not visited.

Wellby presents the clue and the group inspects its language and date pattern. One passage retains the whole exchange. Interacted and supporting are appropriate, and the introduction quote is exact Wellby speech. No translated contents from the reference page have been imported.

Delwath’s room search produces an explicitly magical scroll whose spell is unknown. This is an eligible discovery rather than routine gear use. The single passage preserves search context; the exact DM introduction quote carries the whole polished-turn UID mapping.

scenes.aiSummary: The party smashes a rusty lock to enter the underground passage.
The party follows the connector tunnel and climbs toward a storeroom beneath the fort.
Wellby reports his scouting discoveries; the party examines a logbook and plans routes through the fort.
The party advances through the tunnel while Delwath prepares to scout invisibly.
Delwath scouts the cavern and discovers two ghoul-like hobgoblins.
Delwath returns to the intersection and heads toward the northern rubble passage.

scenes.aiSummary: Delwath observes the plaza through rubble and studies a route outside.

scenes.aiSummary: Delwath scouts the bridge and tower entrances beyond a barred southern gate.

scenes.locationDetail: Tunnel near the shaft and storeroom
scenes.aiSummary: The party compares routes and plans to eliminate the ghouls quietly.
The party approaches the prison cavern for an ambush.
The party kills the two ghouls before they can raise an alarm.
The party examines the execution chamber and considers routes, noises, and places to rest.

scenes.locationDetail: Tunnels leading to the northern and southern watchpoints
scenes.aiSummary: The party divides between two watchpoints for a short rest.
The northern watch observes movement and activity outside during the short rest.

scenes.aiSummary: The southern watch studies the towers and hears activity as the light fades.
scenes.time: During the same short rest, with fading light.

scenes.aiSummary: The party regroups and plans Kenzo’s invisible scouting of the towers.

scenes.locationDetail: First tower, second-floor entrance and windows
scenes.aiSummary: Kenzo enters the first tower and surveys its surroundings.
Kenzo investigates the upper passage and the way toward the next tower.
Kenzo finds an abandoned apartment marked with the Blackened Claw symbol.
Kenzo checks the tower’s remaining routes and exits.
Kenzo returns to gather the party into the first tower.

scenes.locationDetail: Barred overhead gate and passage into the first tower
scenes.aiSummary: The companions move through the gate to search the tower.
Delwath searches the old captain’s apartment and discovers an unidentified magical scroll hidden in the desk.

scenes.locationDetail: Second tower, entrance and third-floor living quarters
scenes.aiSummary: Kenzo scouts the second tower and sees a cloaked orc carrying a scimitar.
Kenzo discovers the injured prisoner Vola, frees her hands, and quietly discusses a rescue.
Kenzo briefly checks the guards’ positions downstairs.
Kenzo returns to reassure Vola and gives her a healing potion.
Kenzo reports the prisoner and guards; the party prepares a rescue assault.

scenes.locationDetail: Second tower approach and third-floor stairs
scenes.aiSummary: The party approaches the guards’ floor in the second tower.
The party sleeps one guard, battles a shapeshifter and the orc spellcaster, and kills the two active opponents.
The party secures the sleeping guard and searches the rooms, finding Vola’s belongings.

scenes.locationDetail: Second tower, fourth-floor prison and stairs
scenes.aiSummary: Kenzo collects Vola and brings her toward the party.
Vola reclaims her gear and advises killing the captive shapeshifter before the party relocates.

scenes.locationDetail: Crossing back to the first tower
scenes.aiSummary: The party escorts Vola to the first tower and bars the door.
Vola explains the Society’s relic hunt, Agata’s involvement, and her connection to Arcus; the party discusses escaping together.
